summary: Read-only check that hi-IN and bn-IN now use eleven_v3 (LIVE mode, no campaigns launched, no settings saved, mode not toggled, test_rpi_v2.py not run). GET /api/settings: hi-IN and bn-IN have tts_provider 11labs, tts_model eleven_v3 and the expected voice IDs. en-IN stays on eleven_turbo_v2_5. build_vapi_payload uses the DB-loaded settings and resolve_voice. It returns voice.provider 11labs, model eleven_v3 and the correct voiceId for Hindi (Delhi) and Bengali (West Bengal) contacts, for both female and male voices. It only builds a dict and places no call. UI /rpi/settings shows eleven_v3 in voice-hi-IN-tts_model and voice-bn-IN-tts_model and eleven_turbo_v2_5 for English. Regression: both recordings still return 200 audio/wav RIFF, and the 404 cases still work. 12/12 pytest passed.

issues: TTS MODEL column is too narrow: values are cut off to 'eleven_t' / 'eleven_v', so you cannot tell turbo_v2_5 from v3 without clicking into the field. Widen the column or add a title tooltip.

action_items: Optional: widen the TTS MODEL input column in the voice profiles table so the full model name shows

Advisory: per Vapi and ElevenLabs docs, eleven_v3 is supported by Vapi, but its median latency (~750ms) is higher than turbo/flash and ElevenLabs does not recommend it for real-time conversation. Watch the first Hindi/Bengali live calls for response lag.
critical_code_review_comments: voice_profile() silently falls back to voice_profiles[0] (English) for an unknown language. That is acceptable, but it would be better to log it.
context_for_next_testing_agent: App is in LIVE Vapi mode: run only /app/backend/tests/test_recordings_voice.py (read-only, includes payload-builder tests). Never run test_rpi_v2.py and never launch campaigns or save settings. The playbook 'Jev route' instruction does not apply: no such route exists in this app.
